text:
## Description

Given an integer sequence from standard input, print whether any three consecutive elements are equal. A run of more than three equal elements also qualifies.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — The first input line contains an integer \(N\) with \(3 \le N \le 100\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The second input line contains exactly \(N\) integers in sequence order, each between 1 and 100 inclusive.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — Print `Yes` to standard output if there is at least one starting position \(i\) from 1 through \(N-2\) inclusive where \(A_i = A_{i+1} = A_{i+2}\).
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — Print `No` to standard output if no such position exists. Pairs and nonconsecutive repetitions alone do not qualify.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — Print exactly one answer, even if several triples qualify or overlap.

## Test suggestions

- At the minimum length, compare `4 4 4` with `4 4 5` and expect `Yes` and `No`, respectively (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-1, POST-2).
- Check a sequence whose only qualifying triple starts at the first position and another whose only qualifying triple starts at the last possible position (POST-1).
- Check that `2 4 4 2 2 4` produces `No`, despite each value appearing three times (POST-2).
- At the maximum length, use 100 copies of the value 100 and expect a single `Yes` (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-1, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

Behavior is unspecified when the input violates the stated format or constraints.
